steps.title: TDN
steps.body: Aged Riesling often smells of petrol, kerosene or rubber. The compound is TDN, 1,1,6-trimethyl-1,2-dihydronaphthalene. It forms from carotenoids in the grape skins, more so with strong sunlight, heat, drought and low yields. Australian Riesling, under intense sun, often shows it early. Some love it; others find it a flaw in excess.

steps.title: How it ages
steps.body: Young Riesling shows fresh lime, apple and flowers. With 5 to 10 years, it gains honey, toast, beeswax and dried apricot, and colour deepens to gold. High acidity preserves it: good dry Riesling ages 15 to 20 years; sweet Auslese and TBA can age 50 years or more.

steps.prompt: What favours the formation of TDN in Riesling?
steps.explanation: Sun exposure increases carotenoids, which become TDN.

steps.body: If you dislike strong petrol notes, look for Riesling from cooler sites, like the Mosel. Hotter, sunnier regions tend to show more TDN.

steps.prompt: Good sweet Riesling can age for 50 years or more.
steps.explanation: Yes. Sugar and high acidity preserve it.

steps.title: What you learned
points: TDN gives aged Riesling its petrol note, more with sun
With age, Riesling gains honey, toast and beeswax
Dry Riesling ages 15 to 20 years; sweet styles 50 or more
